doc.title: John Altman interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, September 14, 2023

title: Copyist errors and Gil Evans's parts
summary: Mistakes in parts, Gil Evans's uncorrected parts and the trumpet player told to play two octaves lower.

story.theme_name: Writing and arranging: how musicians compose
story.community_name: Writing, arranging and composing: how the music gets made

blocks.x: Do you ever walk around the orchestra when they’re rehearsing and you’re hearing something that’s awry.

Totally. It happens quite frequently. You know it’s not so prevalent these days because now music copying is off Sibelius and very rarely things go down incorrectly. I mean I was always amazed to see, years ago, Gil Evans’ parts and there are mistakes still there on the parts. “Oh, that’s not right.” You know, nobody’s ever bothered to correct it. Maybe they did in their head but they haven’t corrected it on the paper.

That makes me think, someone I interviewed recently was talking about the Gil Evans sound and the fact — and he said, “Well he wrote half steps in the middle of the chord sometimes.” Now I’m starting to think well maybe not on purpose.
Well I’ll never forget when he was rehearsing in London the trumpet player said, “Gil my part is a bit high.” And Gil said to him, “Oh, play it two octaves lower then.” Wonderful.
